events.note: NASA P1 08:44:22 UT (https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/LEplot/LEplot2001/LE2026Mar03T.pdf); the Moon has been up since USNO's moonrise at 22:15 UT on 2 March
USNO moonset 11:33 UT ends the eclipse for Philadelphia, before P4 at 14:22:59. Greatest eclipse (11:33:37 UT) falls within a minute of moonset, so the local maximum is not asserted either way
The local span runs from P1 to moonset

name: The total lunar eclipse of 3 March 2026 seen from Philadelphia, cut short by moonset
